claim: Percutaneous needle electrolysis consists of the application of a galvanic current and is an emerging treatment for tendinopathies.
source: Percutaneous needle electrolysis consists of the application of a galvanic current and is an emerging treatment for tendinopathies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a factual statement about the treatment method.

claim: Galvanic current activates the NLRP3 inflammasome in mice.
source: In the present study, we found that galvanic current activates the NLRP3 inflammasome and induces an inflammatory response that promotes a collagen-mediated regeneration of the tendon in mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Galvanic current induces an inflammatory response that promotes collagen-mediated regeneration of the tendon in mice.
source: In the present study, we found that galvanic current activates the NLRP3 inflammasome and induces an inflammatory response that promotes a collagen-mediated regeneration of the tendon in mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Galvanic current applied using a percutaneous needle is a minimally invasive technique that seeks to regenerate damaged tissues.
source: Galvanic current applied using a percutaneous needle is an emerging and minimally invasive technique that seeks to regenerate damaged tissues (Valera-Garrido et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The needle used to apply galvanic current is guided using ultrasound equipment into affected soft tissues by direct visualization.
source: The needle used to apply galvanic current is guided, using ultrasound equipment, into affected soft tissues by direct visualization and therefore is able to stimulate locally the cells in the damaged area.
evidence: This is a description of the technique stated in the introduction.

claim: Percutaneous needle electrolysis combines mechanical and electrical stimulation of the tissue that results in a local controlled microtrauma.
source: Percutaneous needle electrolysis consists of applying a galvanic current through an acupuncture needle and thus combining mechanical and electrical stimulation of the tissue that results in a local controlled microtrauma.
evidence: This is a description of the mechanism stated in the introduction.

claim: The microtrauma generated by percutaneous needle electrolysis generates a local inflammatory response that makes possible and fosters the repair of the affected tissue.
source: This microtrauma in turn generates a local inflammatory response that makes possible and fosters the repair of the affected tissue (Valera-Garrido and Minaya-Muñoz, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Galvanic current has been successfully used to repair chronic non-resolving lesions, such as tendinopathies developed after prolonged extreme exercise.
source: Galvanic current has been successfully used to repair chronic non-resolving lesions, such as tendinopathies developed after prolonged extreme exercise, which often establish a degenerative condition of the tissue that impairs healing and complicates clinical management (Cook and Purdam, 2009; Regan et al., 1992; Soslowsky et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Tendinopathies developed after prolonged extreme exercise often establish a degenerative condition of the tissue that impairs healing and complicates clinical management.
source: Galvanic current has been successfully used to repair chronic non-resolving lesions, such as tendinopathies developed after prolonged extreme exercise, which often establish a degenerative condition of the tissue that impairs healing and complicates clinical management (Cook and Purdam, 2009; Regan et al., 1992; Soslowsky et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In randomized trials, anti-inflammatory therapies have shown to be ineffectual at treating tendinopathy lesions.
source: In randomized trials, anti-inflammatory therapies have shown to be ineffectual at treating these types of lesion (Bisset et al., 2006; Coombes et al., 2013) and application of galvanic currents by percutaneous needle alone has been found sufficient when it comes to regenerating the tissue (Bubnov et al., 2013; Chellini et al., 2019; De-la-Cruz-Torres et al., 2020; Margalef et al., 2020; Valera-Garrido et al., 2020; Valera-Garrido et al., 2014; Valera-Garrido et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous randomized trials.

claim: Application of galvanic currents by percutaneous needle alone has been found sufficient for regenerating tendon tissue.
source: In randomized trials, anti-inflammatory therapies have shown to be ineffectual at treating these types of lesion (Bisset et al., 2006; Coombes et al., 2013) and application of galvanic currents by percutaneous needle alone has been found sufficient when it comes to regenerating the tissue (Bubnov et al., 2013; Chellini et al., 2019; De-la-Cruz-Torres et al., 2020; Margalef et al., 2020; Valera-Garrido et al., 2020; Valera-Garrido et al., 2014; Valera-Garrido et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Resolving inflammation promotes a response that recovers homeostasis by repairing tissues.
source: Resolving inflammation promotes a response that recovers homeostasis by repairing tissues (Medzhitov, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Chronic non-resolving inflammation can induce continuous tissue regeneration and excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix components, which leads to fibrosis of soft tissues.
source: However, chronic non-resolving inﬂammation can induce continuous tissue regeneration and excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix components, which in turn leads to fibrosis of soft tissues (Alegre et al., 2017; Borthwick et al., 2013; Gaul et al., 2021; Wynn, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A balanced inflammatory response is required to recover homeostasis and successfully heal tissue.
source: Therefore, a balanced inflammatory response is required to recover homeostasis and successfully heal tissue (Borthwick et al., 2013; Eming et al., 2017; Liston and Masters, 2017; Medzhitov, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In response to tissue damage, the NLRP3 inflammasome is specifically activated over other inflammatory pathways and coordinates an inflammatory response.
source: In response to tissue damage, the nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain with leucine-rich repeat and pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is specifically activated over other inflammatory pathways and coordinates an inflammatory response (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Schroder and Tschopp, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: NLRP3 inflammasome is a multiprotein complex induced in myeloid cells after the detection of damage- or pathogen-associated molecular patterns.
source: NLRP3 inflammasome is a multiprotein complex induced in myeloid cells after the detection of damage- or pathogen-associated molecular patterns, including elevated concentrations of extracellular ATP, changes in extracellular osmolarity or detection of insoluble particles and crystals, such as uric acid crystals or amyloid deposition (Amores-Iniesta et al., 2017; Compan et al., 2012; Heneka et al., 2013; Martinon et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: NLRP3 triggers specifically induce NLRP3 activation over other inflammasomes as they decrease intracellular K+ concentration resulting in conformational change of NLRP3 structure.
source: These triggers specifically induce NLRP3 activation over other inflammasomes as they decrease intracellular K+ concentration resulting in conformational change of NLRP3 structure and, therefore, active NLRP3 oligomers (Munoz-Planillo et al., 2013; Tapia-Abellán et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Active NLRP3 oligomers recruit the accessory apoptosis-speck-like protein with a caspase recruitment and activation domain (ASC) that favors the activation of the inflammatory caspase-1.
source: Active NLRP3 oligomers recruit the accessory apoptosis-speck-like protein with a caspase recruitment and activation domain (ASC) that favors the activation of the inflammatory caspase-1 (Boucher et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018; Schmidt et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Caspase-1 proteolytically processes immature pro-inflammatory cytokines of the interleukin (IL)–1 family to produce the bioactive form of IL-1β and IL-18.
source: Caspase-1 proteolytically processes immature pro-inflammatory cytokines of the interleukin (IL)–1 family to produce the bioactive form of IL-1β and IL-18 (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Schroder and Tschopp, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Caspase-1 processes gasdermin D protein (GSDMD), and its amino-terminal fragment (GSDMDNT) oligomerizes in the plasma membrane forming pores.
source: Caspase-1 also processes gasdermin D protein (GSDMD), and its amino-terminal fragment (GSDMDNT) oligomerizes in the plasma membrane forming pores, thus releasing IL-1β and IL-18 cytokines, as well as other intracellular content, including inflammasome oligomers (Baroja-Mazo et al., 2014; Broz et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: GSDMDNT pores release IL-1β and IL-18 cytokines, as well as other intracellular content, including inflammasome oligomers.
source: Caspase-1 also processes gasdermin D protein (GSDMD), and its amino-terminal fragment (GSDMDNT) oligomerizes in the plasma membrane forming pores, thus releasing IL-1β and IL-18 cytokines, as well as other intracellular content, including inflammasome oligomers (Baroja-Mazo et al., 2014; Broz et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Prolonged NLRP3 activation occurs in different chronic inflammatory, metabolic and degenerative diseases such as gout, type 2 diabetes or Alzheimer.
source: Prolonged NLRP3 activation occurs in different chronic inflammatory, metabolic and degenerative diseases such as gout, type 2 diabetes or Alzheimer (Daniels et al., 2016; Heneka et al., 2013; Masters et al., 2010; Martinon et al., 2006), therefore selective small molecules that block NLRP3 are emerging as novel anti-inflammatory therapies (Cocco et al., 2017; Coll et al., 2015; Tapia-Abellán et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Selective small molecules that block NLRP3 are emerging as novel anti-inflammatory therapies.
source: Prolonged NLRP3 activation occurs in different chronic inflammatory, metabolic and degenerative diseases such as gout, type 2 diabetes or Alzheimer (Daniels et al., 2016; Heneka et al., 2013; Masters et al., 2010; Martinon et al., 2006), therefore selective small molecules that block NLRP3 are emerging as novel anti-inflammatory therapies (Cocco et al., 2017; Coll et al., 2015; Tapia-Abellán et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Immunosuppressed septic patients have high mortality rates due to secondary infections associated with a profound deactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: However, in some pathological circumstances, a boost, rather than an inhibition, of NLRP3 would be more beneficial for reducing clinical complications, such as in immunosuppressed septic patients, who have high mortality rates due to secondary infections associated with a profound deactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome (Martinez-García et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Applying 12 mA of galvanic current twice for 6 s each time to LPS stimulated macrophages increases the expression of Cox2 and Il6 genes.
source: Applying 12 mA of galvanic current twice for 6 s each time to LPS stimulated macrophages increase the expression of Cox2 and Il6 genes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Galvanic current does not affect LPS-induced Il1b or Tnfa pro-inflammatory gene expression.
source: However, it did not affect LPS-induced Il1b or Tnfa pro-inflammatory gene expression (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Tnfa expression was upregulated with galvanic current alone.
source: Interestingly, meanwhile Tnfa expression was upregulated with galvanic current alone (Figure 1A), galvanic currents did not induce the expression of Cox2, Il6 or Il1b genes on non-LPS-treated macrophages, or over IL-4-treated macrophages (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Galvanic currents did not induce the expression of Cox2, Il6 or Il1b genes on non-LPS-treated macrophages, or over IL-4-treated macrophages.
source: Interestingly, meanwhile Tnfa expression was upregulated with galvanic current alone (Figure 1A), galvanic currents did not induce the expression of Cox2, Il6 or Il1b genes on non-LPS-treated macrophages, or over IL-4-treated macrophages (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: When macrophages were polarized to M2 by IL-4, galvanic currents decreased the expression of the M2 markers Arg1, Fizz1, and Mrc1.
source: When macrophages were polarized to M2 by IL-4, galvanic currents decreased the expression of the M2 markers Arg1, Fizz1, and Mrc1 (Figure 1B); however, this decrease was small and non-significant for the M2 marker Ym1 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Galvanic current did not increase the concentration of IL-6 or TNF-α released after LPS stimulation.
source: We next studied the concentration of released pro-inflammatory cytokines from macrophages, and found that galvanic current did not increase the concentration of IL-6 or TNF-α released after LPS stimulation (Figure 1C), but that it did significantly augment the release of IL-1β in an intensity-dependent manner (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Galvanic current significantly augments the release of IL-1β in an intensity-dependent manner.
source: We next studied the concentration of released pro-inflammatory cytokines from macrophages, and found that galvanic current did not increase the concentration of IL-6 or TNF-α released after LPS stimulation (Figure 1C), but that it did significantly augment the release of IL-1β in an intensity-dependent manner (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Casp1/11-/- macrophages fail to release IL-1β induced by galvanic current.
source: We found that Casp1/11-/- macrophages fail to release IL-1β induced by galvanic current (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Applying galvanic current to Pycard-/- macrophages failed to induce the release of IL-1β, indicating that the inflammasome adaptor protein ASC is needed to activate the inflammasome.
source: We then found that applying galvanic current to Pycard-/- macrophages also failed to induce the release of IL-1β, which indicated that the inflammasome adaptor protein ASC is also needed to activate the inflammasome (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Nlrp3-/- and the use of the specific NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950 impaired the release of IL-1β induced by galvanic current.
source: Nlrp3-/- and the use of the specific NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950 (Coll et al., 2015; Tapia-Abellán et al., 2019) impaired the release of IL-1β induced by galvanic current (Figure 2A and B), demonstrating that the NLRP3 inflammasome is activated when galvanic current is applied.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Galvanic current was able to induce the release of IL-18.
source: Similarly, galvanic current was also able to induce the release of IL-18 (Figure 2C), another cytokine dependent on the activation of the inflammasome.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The use of MCC950 or macrophages deficient in NLRP3 failed to release IL-18 after galvanic current was applied.
source: The use of MCC950 or macrophages deficient in NLRP3 failed to release IL-18 after galvanic current was applied (Figure 2C), which confirms that galvanic current stimulates NLRP3 to induce the release of both IL-1β and IL-18.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The use of an extracellular buffer with 40 mM of KCl decreased IL-1β release induced by nigericin and galvanic current application, but not the release of IL-1β induced by Clostridium difficile toxin B.
source: Mechanistically, the use of an extracellular buffer with 40 mM of KCl decreased IL-1β release induced by nigericin and galvanic current application, but not the release of IL-1β induced by Clostridium difficile toxin B, which activates the Pyrin inflammasome, which is a K+-efflux independent inflammasome (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Two pulses of 12 mA of galvanic current for 6 s failed to decrease intracellular K+.
source: However, two pulses of 12 mA of galvanic current for 6 s failed to decrease intracellular K+ (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), but increasing the number of pulses of galvanic current to eight did result in a significant decrease of intracellular K+ (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Increasing the number of pulses of galvanic current to eight resulted in a significant decrease of intracellular K+.
source: However, two pulses of 12 mA of galvanic current for 6 s failed to decrease intracellular K+ (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), but increasing the number of pulses of galvanic current to eight did result in a significant decrease of intracellular K+ (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: After applying galvanic current, the generation of the active p20 caspase-1 fragment, and processed IL-1β and GSDMDNT were detected.
source: After applying galvanic current we were able to detect the generation of the active p20 caspase-1 fragment, and processed IL-1β and GSDMDNT (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: MCC950 was able to abrogate caspase-1 activation and the processed forms of IL-1β and GSDMDNT.
source: MCC950 was able to abrogate caspase-1 activation and the processed forms of IL-1β and GSDMDNT (Figure 2F), which suggests functional activation of caspase-1 and downstream signaling because of the activation of canonical NLRP3 and rules out the non-canonical NLRP3 activation that would result in GSDMD processing in the presence of MCC950.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: 2 impacts of 12 mA of galvanic current for 6 s induced the formation of an intracellular NLRP3–YFP punctum, which was inhibited by the application of MCC950.
source: Fluorescence microscopy showed that 2 impacts of 12 mA of galvanic current for 6 s induced the formation of an intracellular NLRP3–YFP punctum, which was inhibited by the application of MCC950 (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Two impacts of galvanic currents of different intensities (3, 6, 12 mA) for a period of 6 s only induced a slight increase in cell death.
source: Two impacts of galvanic currents of different intensities (3, 6, 12 mA) for a period of 6 s (conditions that induce IL-1β release as we show in Figure 1C) only induced a slight increase in cell death (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The increase in cell death induced by galvanic current was not associated with the activation of the inflammasome given that it was also present in macrophages deficient in NLRP3, ASC or caspase-1/11.
source: This increase in cell death was not associated with the activation of the inflammasome given that it was also present in macrophages deficient in NLRP3, ASC or caspase-1/11 (Figure 3B), which in turn suggests that it occurred independently of inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Increasing the number or the length of time of 12 mA impacts of galvanic current on macrophages resulted in a time-dependent increase in cell death.
source: Increasing the number or the length of time of 12 mA impacts of galvanic current on macrophages, resulted in a time-dependent increase in cell death (Figure 3A), which correlates with higher concentrations of IL-1β and IL-18 release (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3C.

claim: IL-1β and IL-18 release was blocked by MCC950, but LDH release was not dependent on NLRP3 activation.
source: However, whereas IL-1β and IL-18 release was blocked by MCC950 (Figure 3C), LDH release was not dependent on NLRP3 activation (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Two impacts of 12 mA for a period of 6 s were unable to induce plasma membrane permeabilization measured in terms of Yo-Pro-1 uptake during a period of 3 h.
source: Similarly, two impacts of 12 mA for a period of 6 s were unable to induce plasma membrane permeabilization measured in terms of Yo-Pro-1 uptake during a period of 3 h (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Yo-Pro uptake increased over 3 h in an intensity dependent manner (3, 6, 12 mA) when eight impacts were applied for 6 s.
source: Yo-Pro uptake increased over 3 h in an intensity dependent manner (3, 6, 12 mA) when eight impacts were applied for 6 s (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The increase in plasma membrane permeabilization was not reversed after NLRP3 was blocked with MCC950 or when ASC-deficient macrophages were used.
source: This increase in plasma membrane permeabilization was not reversed after NLRP3 was blocked with MCC950 or when ASC-deficient macrophages were used (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Application of 3 impacts of 3 mA of galvanic current for 3 s in the calcaneal tendon of mice increased the number of polymorphonuclear cells after 3 days when compared with tendons treated with needling alone.
source: When studying the effect of galvanic current in vivo, we found that application of 3 impacts of 3 mA of galvanic current for 3 s in the calcaneal tendon of mice increased the number of polymorphonuclear cells after 3 days when compared with tendons treated with needling alone (a puncture without current application, Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The increase in polymorphonuclear cells returned to basal after 7 days and stayed low up to 21 days after galvanic current application.
source: This increase returned to basal after 7 days and stayed low up to 21 days after galvanic current application (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The number of F4/80+ macrophages increased 3 days after the application of galvanic current when compared to needling alone and returned to basal levels after 7 days.
source: Similarly, the number of F4/80+ macrophages increased 3 days after the application of galvanic current when compared to needling alone and returned to basal levels after 7 days (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The application of galvanic current to LPS-primed neutrophils failed to release IL-1β or LDH.
source: However, the application of galvanic current to LPS-primed neutrophils failed to release IL-1β or LDH (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Expression of Il6, Il1a, and Il1b, as well as the IL-1 receptor antagonist (Il1rn) and the chemokine Cxcl10 all increased after percutaneous electrolysis when compared to needling alone.
source: Expression of Il6, Il1a, and Il1b, as well as the IL-1 receptor antagonist (Il1rn) and the chemokine Cxcl10 all increased after percutaneous electrolysis when compared to needling alone (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Different NLRP3 inflammasome genes (Nlrp3, Pycard, Casp1) exhibit an increase in expression when galvanic current was applied, but this increase was not significant when compared to needling.
source: Different NLRP3 inflammasome genes also exhibit an increase in expression (Nlrp3, Pycard, Casp1) when galvanic current was applied, but this increase was not significant when compared to needling (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Gsdmd expression was not upregulated in the tendons after galvanic current application.
source: Gsdmd expression was not upregulated in the tendons after galvanic current application (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Application of 3 impacts of 3 mA of galvanic current for 3 s in the calcaneal tendon of Nlrp3-/- mice resulted in a significant reduction of Il1b, Il1rn and Cxcl10 expression after 3 days when compared to wild type mice.
source: Application of 3 impacts of 3 mA of galvanic current for 3 s in the calcaneal tendon of Nlrp3-/- mice resulted in a significant reduction of Il1b, Il1rn and Cxcl10 expression after 3 days when compared to wild type mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Specific inflammasome associated genes, such as Pycard, Casp1, or Gsdmd (except for Nlrp3) did not affect their expression in the calcaneal tendon of Nlrp3-/- mice 3 days after the application of galvanic current when compared to wild type mice.
source: Specific inflammasome associated genes, such as Pycard, Casp1, or Gsdmd (except for Nlrp3) did not affect their expression in the calcaneal tendon of Nlrp3-/- mice 3 days after the application of galvanic current when compared to wild type mice (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Galvanic current tended to increase the expression of Il6 in the tendons of Nlrp3-/- after 3 days.
source: Surprisingly, galvanic current tended to increase both the expression of Il6 in the tendons of Nlrp3-/- after 3 days (Figure 6C) and the number of polymorphonuclear cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Galvanic current tended to increase the number of polymorphonuclear cells in Nlrp3-/- mice.
source: Surprisingly, galvanic current tended to increase both the expression of Il6 in the tendons of Nlrp3-/- after 3 days (Figure 6C) and the number of polymorphonuclear cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The number of macrophages was not affected in the Nlrp3-/- calcaneal tendon when galvanic current was applied.
source: However, the number of macrophages was not affected in the Nlrp3-/- calcaneal tendon when galvanic current was applied (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: A decrease in Il1b and Cxcl10 expression was confirmed in the tendons of Pycard-/- mice 3 days after the application of galvanic current.
source: We also confirmed a decrease in Il1b and Cxcl10 expression in the tendons of Pycard-/- mice 3 days after the application of galvanic current (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B), which suggests that the NLRP3 inflammasome is important in modulating part of the inflammatory response after the application of galvanic current.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: The expression of Tgfb1 3 days after the application of galvanic current in the calcaneal tendon of mice was dependent on NLRP3.
source: We found that in vivo the expression of Tgfb1 3 days after the application of galvanic current in the calcaneal tendon of mice was dependent on NLRP3 (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: After 7 days of percutaneous electrolysis the levels of type III collagen were decreased, with a parallel increase in type I collagen when compared to needling alone.
source: Likewise, after 7 days of percutaneous electrolysis the levels of type III collagen were decreased, with a parallel increase in type I collagen when compared to needling alone (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Percutaneous electrolysis did not affect collagen fiber properties (width or length) when compared to needling alone.
source: However, percutaneous electrolysis did not affect collagen fiber properties (width or length) when compared to needling alone (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The increase in type I collagen 7 days after galvanic current application was reduced in Nlrp3-/- mice.
source: The increase in type I collagen 7 days after galvanic current application was reduced in Nlrp3-/- mice (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: NLRP3 controlled the structural dispersion of collagen fibers, which was decreased by galvanic current application in wild type mice, but increased in Nlrp3-/- mice.
source: NLRP3 also controlled the structural dispersion of collagen fibers, which was decreased by galvanic current application in wild type mice, but increased in Nlrp3-/- mice (Figure 7D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Controlled deposition of collagen fibers induced by galvanic current increased tendon stiffness and decreased the maximum tension supported by the tendon.
source: This controlled deposition of collagen fibers induced by galvanic current increased tendon stiffness and decreased the maximum tension supported by the tendon (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: NLRP3 inflammasome was responsible for increased tendon stiffness after galvanic current application.
source: NLRP3 inflammasome was responsible for increased tendon stiffness after galvanic current application (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Galvanic current could enhance the pro-inflammatory signature of M1 macrophages whilst decreasing M2 polarization.
source: These data suggest that galvanic current could enhance the pro-inflammatory signature of M1 macrophages whilst decreasing M2 polarization.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: The increase in Il6 and Tnfa gene expression detected at mRNA level does not transcribe to higher release of IL-6 and TNF-α over LPS treatment.
source: These data indicate that the increase in Il6 and Tnfa gene expression detected at mRNA level does not transcribe to higher release of IL-6 and TNF-α over LPS treatment, but that galvanic current could potentially activate an inflammasome that induces the release of IL-1β.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Galvanic current could potentially activate an inflammasome that induces the release of IL-1β.
source: These data indicate that the increase in Il6 and Tnfa gene expression detected at mRNA level does not transcribe to higher release of IL-6 and TNF-α over LPS treatment, but that galvanic current could potentially activate an inflammasome that induces the release of IL-1β.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Galvanic current activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, and no other inflammasome expressed in the macrophages was being activated.
source: All these data confirm that galvanic current activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, and since NLRP3-deficient macrophages failed to release IL-1β or IL-18, that no other inflammasome expressed in the macrophages was being activated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Galvanic current slightly decreases intracellular K+ when compared to the application of the K+ ionophore nigericin.
source: These data suggest that galvanic current slightly decreases intracellular K+ when compared to the application of the K+ ionophore nigericin (Figure 2E) and this explains the smaller concentration of IL-1β that is released by galvanic current compared to nigericin application (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 2E and 2B.

claim: The smaller concentration of IL-1β released by galvanic current compared to nigericin application is explained by galvanic current slightly decreasing intracellular K+.

claim: Galvanic current application could result in two potentially different mechanisms: (i) an alternative means of processing GSDMD occurs which is independent of NLRP3 and which could inactivate its N-terminal lytic domain, or (ii) small amounts of GSDMDNT create a small number of pores in the plasma membrane, facilitating their repair and leading to a hyperactive state of the macrophage.
